See our privacy policy . Common questions before you start Can I build a retaining wall myself or do I need a licensed builder? Homeowners often build small, non‑structural garden walls themselves using blocks, sleepers or DIY kits. For larger structural walls, especially those above around a metre or retaining driveways and buildings, NSW regulations usually require licensed contractors and, in some cases, engineers. Insurance and future resale can be affected if the wall is not built by appropriately qualified trades. Many people in Newcastle choose to DIY only the very small decorative walls and leave the bigger ones to professionals. How high can I build a retaining wall without an engineer in NSW? In much of NSW, including Newcastle, simple low walls can sometimes be built without an engineer, but anything over roughly 1–1.5 metres typically needs engineering design and certification. Height isn’t the only factor; soil type, loads above the wall and proximity to boundaries also matter. Councils and certifiers look at whether the wall is retaining more than just garden soil, such as driveways or structures. When in doubt, homeowners usually engage an engineer to avoid safety and compliance issues. Do retaining walls need drainage behind them? Yes, almost all retaining walls need proper drainage to stay stable and avoid damage. Builders usually install gravel backfill, ag pipe and weep holes to let water escape rather than build up pressure behind the wall.
